source.examples_from: https://personalagentprotocol.org/docs/0.4/spec.md (sha256 b65e9620fd777a214e73e923f8e17691be390fcc07c5dd4e21c3707c8468a967), each JSON code block as published, keyed by section and its place in that section. The 5.2 Session JWT block is a header and a payload separated by a line holding ".", stored here as {header, payload}.
source.note: Copied as published; nothing edited. The project checks every JSON example in the spec against these schemas in its own build (lib/kit/examples.ts).

scopes.orders:read: See your orders, returns, and bookings
scopes.orders:write: Exchange or return items, and change bookings
scopes.addresses: See and change your saved shipping addresses
scopes.poppy:browser-sign-in: Use the website signed in, with the other access you approve

authorization-server-metadata.schema.jso.title: OAuth Authorization Server Metadata
authorization-server-metadata.schema.jso.description: The RFC 8414 metadata the Company's issuer publishes, with the fields Poppy requires. Spec section 3.2 (OAuth server). Other fields are allowed, and Personal Agents ignore them. grant_types_supported says which of Direct and Device Sign-In the Company offers: authorization_endpoint is required when it includes authorization_code, and device_authorization_endpoint when it includes the device_code grant. Publishing scopes_supported and a complete scope inventory is recommended. Endpoint conditions and scope recommendations are checked separately.

token_endpoint_auth_signing_alg_values_s.description: RFC 8414 section 2. Accepted client-assertion algorithms, not delegation algorithms. Poppy requires ES256 and recommends PS384.

grant_types_supported.description: Must include refresh_token, which is checked separately.

protected_resources.description: RFC 9728 section 4. Lists https://{domain} for every domain whose issuer it is, and may list other resources.

poppy.schema.json.title: poppy.json
poppy.schema.json.description: The discovery document a Company publishes at /.well-known/poppy.json. Spec section 3 (Discovery) and 3.1 (Fields). Unknown fields are allowed: Personal Agents ignore fields they don't recognize.

supported_versions.description: The other protocol versions the Company serves, each mapped to the HTTPS URL of that version's document, on the host that served poppy.json (spec 3.4). A version's document has no supported_versions.

auth.description: Optional. issuer is required only when the domain's protected resource metadata lists more than one authorization server, and must then be one of them (spec 3.1, 3.2), which is checked separately.

disabled.description: true if the Company offers Personal Agents no sign-in, even though it has an issuer (spec 3.2).

scopes.description: Scope descriptions, keyed by scope name, in the same form as an OpenAPI OAuth 2.0 security scheme. Describing offered scopes here or in a listed OpenAPI description is recommended.

scope_hints.description: Hints about each scope, keyed by scope name, describing the most consequential operation that requires it.

access.description: For a poppy protocol entry, session (the default) or signed_in. Unknown values are ignored as an absent hint (spec 3.2).

disabled.description: true if the Company asks Personal Agents not to browse its website, and to use its Company Agent and APIs instead (spec section 6).

unscoped.description: true if the website doesn't apply the Company's other scopes, so poppy:browser-sign-in gives the account's full access there (spec section 6).

mediated-sign-in.description: The Mediated Sign-In extension (Mediated Sign-In 2), with an entry for each version. Version 1 has the credentials to collect, each sent as a token request parameter of that name, and the scopes it can grant. The grant is at the issuer's token_endpoint, which lists https://personalagentprotocol.org/grant/mediated-sign-in in grant_types_supported.

name.description: Not grant_type, scope, resource, a client authentication parameter such as client_id or client_assertion, or a parameter the extension defines, such as sign_in_id.

extensions.description: The extensions the Company supports, keyed by name, each a list with an entry for each major version (spec 3.3).

protected-resource-metadata.schema.json.title: OAuth Protected Resource Metadata
protected-resource-metadata.schema.json.description: RFC 9728 protected resource metadata, with the fields Poppy needs. The Company's domain publishes it at https://{domain}/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource with resource exactly https://{domain}, and authorization_servers names its issuer when it has one (spec 3.2). An issuerless Company may omit authorization_servers or use an empty array. A listed MCP server publishes it with resource set to its URL and the Company's issuer in authorization_servers (spec 7), as does any service that accepts only tokens issued for it (spec 4.5). Other fields are allowed.

session-jwt.schema.json.title: Session JWT
session-jwt.schema.json.description: The JWT in the Poppy-Session header, as its decoded header and payload (spec 5.2). The Personal Agent signs one for each request with a delegated key: kid is the delegated key's JWK thumbprint, and poppy_dlg is the delegation that vouches for it (delegation.schema.json). The Company verifies it as spec 5.3 describes. agent_id is optional, and ath is present only when the request carries an access token. The header and payload are also available on their own as session-jwt.schema.json#/$defs/header and #/$defs/payload.
